against.text: AARO's Historical Record Report of March 2024 states that it found no empirical evidence of government or private reverse engineering of extraterrestrial technology, that none of its interviewees had first-hand knowledge, that most claims were inaccurate or misidentified authentic programmes, and that the claim is largely the product of circular reporting among a group of believers.

The specimens on the board that have been examined came back ordinary or unresolved: AARO reports that Oak Ridge found conventional aluminium alloy, Puthoff wrote in 2012 that tests on one set of samples had produced no anomalous outcome, and the Nolan and Vallee analysis of the Council Bluffs material found no anomalous isotopic values, only an industrial process of unknown origin.

On KONA BLUE, AARO states that it was a proposed programme never approved, that no extraterrestrial craft or bodies were ever collected, and that the material was only assumed to exist by the programme's advocates.

The Air Force's case on Roswell is that the most likely source of the wreckage was a MOGUL balloon train, and that claims of bodies only became part of the incident after 1978; AARO's Volume I concludes that the Roswell materials were consistent with a Mogul balloon and that there is no evidence the government recovered aliens or extraterrestrial material.

The Department's June 2023 answer to Grusch was that AARO had not discovered any verifiable information substantiating a possession or reverse-engineering programme, and AARO's own file logs nine contacts or attempts between June 2023 and January 2024 to arrange an interview with him, most through intermediaries, and concludes in its words that "Mr. Grusch had no intention of providing AARO with information."
According to AARO's report, the companies named deny it: executives and chief technology officers of the named companies denied the allegations to its Director on the record.

NASA's independent study team reported in September 2023 that it found no evidence of extraterrestrial origin, and Bob Lazar's S-4 claim has a counter-explanation reached by two people by unrelated routes: that S-4 refers to a radar facility, not an underground base.

answer.text: The only official announcement of a recovery on the board is Roswell Army Air Field's of 8 July 1947 that the 509th Bomb Group had come into possession of a flying disc, retracted the same day. The Air Force's 1994 report attributed the debris to Project MOGUL and acknowledged that the weather balloon explanation had been a cover story, and GAO found the base's outgoing messages for 1946 to 1949 destroyed with no disposition authority.

The modern claim is testimony. Grusch testified under oath that he was informed of a crash retrieval and reverse-engineering programme, and that his answer on possession rests on interviewing over 40 witnesses over four years; by his own account he learned of it from others, and he says the witnesses with firsthand knowledge made their own protected disclosures.

AARO's Volume I is the official answer: it states that it found no empirical evidence that the government or private companies reverse-engineered extraterrestrial technology, that none of its interviewees had firsthand knowledge, and that the claims come largely from circular reporting among a group of individuals active since 2009.

Between the two sits the custody gap: the released AAWSAP record documents paper in detail and objects not at all, and on the board's reading the documented chains go dark at a private laboratory outside FOIA and inside an Army research agreement that has published nothing.

The official findings are bounded by access. AARO's corporate findings rest on executives' on-the-record denials and the report describes no inspection of any contractor facility, and on the board's reading NASA's study team saw only unclassified data, so its finding measures its own access.

c-a64ba4a596.text: THE SECOND-BEST FINDING IN THIS CLUSTER: TWO PEOPLE REACH THE SAME COUNTER-EXPLANATION BY UNRELATED ROUTES. Tom Mahood, a physics graduate who spent years on the documentary record, concludes in his 2018 retrospective that there is 'nothing at Papoose Lake' and that S-4 actually refers to a radar facility at the Tonopah Test Range. Separately, T.D. Barnes, a former CIA and NASA engineer who worked at Groom Lake, says the real Site 4 is a remote radar site north of the main facility that held captured Soviet equipment, that this and not an underground base is what Lazar referred to, and that a named retired Area 51 security chief confirmed to him that Lazar appears on no manifest. Neither route depends on the other: one is documentary and civilian, the other is recollection by a former range engineer. Shared conclusions from a shared method are not corroboration; these two do not share a method.

for.text: Grusch testified under oath on 26 July 2023 that in his official duties he was informed of a multi-decade crash retrieval and reverse-engineering programme, was denied the read-ons when he asked, and reported this to his superiors and several inspectors general. This is sworn testimony to what he was told, not a record of the programme.

According to Grusch's sworn testimony and The Debrief, the Inspector General of the Intelligence Community found his urgent-concern complaint credible and urgent in July 2022; the finding is known on the board only through those accounts.

Others support him on the record: Karl Nell called his account of a reverse-engineering arms race fundamentally correct, Christopher Mellon says well-placed officials shared detailed information with him, and Luis Elizondo said under oath in 2024 that he agreed with Grusch's testimony. The board notes that no document establishes whether Mellon's sources and Grusch's overlap, and Nell and Mellon spoke through the same Debrief article that introduced Grusch.

AARO itself confirms that the private organisation owning alleged crash material negotiated an agreement in 2019 with the Army to analyse the samples, under a cooperative research agreement signed on 10 October 2019 covering areas such as inertial mass reduction and metamaterials; in 2020 the Army denied in full a FOIA request for 29 emails of their correspondence.

George Knapp testified under oath in September 2025 that Robert Bigelow and an AAWSAP colleague negotiated with senior Lockheed Martin executives to receive unusual material stored at a facility in California, and Luis Elizondo testified in November 2024 that the reported transfer was blocked and that a Secretary of the Air Force memorandum required to complete it never issued. Both are sworn testimony, not records of the transfer.

On the board's own inference, a KONA BLUE proposal to protect the retrieval and exploitation of non-human biologics shows that its proposers believed such material was already held, a belief AARO answers by saying the material was only assumed to exist; James Lacatski hinted in April 2026 that a smaller effort related to KONA BLUE continued after AAWSAP ended.

Covert recovery of hardware under commercial cover has a documented precedent: the CIA's released history of Project AZORIAN records a Soviet submarine lost in March 1968 and raised in 1974 by a system built for the purpose. It shows the capability, not any non-human object.

lead.text: The allegation that a multi-decade effort has retrieved craft and material and tried to reverse-engineer them rests on testimony, most prominently David Grusch's sworn account of July 2023. AARO says it found no empirical evidence of reverse engineering, and no released AAWSAP-era document records the receipt, transfer or storage of any physical sample.

open: Is there any record, anywhere, of the receipt, transfer or storage of a recovered physical object, as opposed to reports and memoranda about one?
What is the name of the programme Grusch says he was denied access to, which has never been placed on the public record?
What did the Army's cooperative research agreement with To The Stars actually find, and why were its emails withheld in full?
Would any official review with classified access reach the same finding as AARO's Volume I?
Who destroyed the RAAF administrative records and outgoing messages, when, and under what authority?

threads.text: The custody thread follows the allegation from Grusch's sworn testimony to a House Oversight subcommittee, which on the board's reading holds no entitlement under section 119, through AARO's statement that KONA BLUE was never reported to Congress because it was never established as a SAP, to the one documentary link: GAO's 1986 review of special-access document control at the Lockheed/Burbank plant, which found 1,460 discrepancies in about 40,000 secret and top-secret items. The chain documents weak control of classified paper at a contractor, and the step that ties KONA BLUE to Lockheed-held material is an allegation.

title: Has the US recovered non-human craft?
